import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 462

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/462](https://www.erdosproblems.com/462)
-/

namespace Erdos462

open Filter
open scoped BigOperators

/--
Let $p(n)$ denote the least prime factor of $n$. Is there a constant $C>0$ such that
$$\sum_{x\leq n\leq x+C\sqrt{x}(\log x)^2}\frac{p(n)}{n}\gg 1$$
for all sufficiently large $x$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_462 : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ C c : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ 0 < c ∧ ∀ᶠ x : ℕ in atTop,
      c ≤ ∑ n ∈ Finset.Icc x
        ⌊(x : ℝ) + C * Real.sqrt x * (Real.log x) ^ 2⌋₊, (n.minFac : ℝ) / n := by
  sorry

end Erdos462

reformulations.difference: Lean uses natural-number starting points. Reading the source's “for all large x” as allowing real starting points instead gives a sum starting at ceil(x). These formulations are equivalent despite not using exactly the same intervals.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Put g(x)=sqrt(x)(log x)^2. For sufficiently large real x and y=ceil(x), we have x≤y≤x+1≤2x, g(y)≤8g(x), and g(x)≥1. Thus y+Cg(y)≤x+(8C+1)g(x). The integer-starting interval at y is contained in the real-starting interval with constant 8C+1. All summands are nonnegative, so the same positive lower bound transfers. Conversely, the real-starting statement restricts directly to natural starting points. The floored upper bounds select exactly the integers satisfying the source's upper inequality. The full equivalence was proved in /workspace/review/equivalence.lean without using the conjecture or any sorry axioms.
